stories.title: The king and AI: U.K. monarch Charles meets with artificial intelligence leaders
stories.simple_summary: The King of the United Kingdom met with people who lead AI companies to discuss artificial intelligence.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and politicians — it shows governments are paying attention to AI, but nothing changes for you today.

stories.title: King Charles warns AI leaders of 'existential dangers'
stories.simple_summary: King Charles told AI leaders that he's worried artificial intelligence could cause serious problems in the future.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and politicians — it's a signal that world leaders want AI companies to be more careful.

stories.title: Bots Behaving Badly? New York Wants to Hear From A.I. Whistle-Blowers.
stories.simple_summary: New York State is asking people who work at AI companies to report if they see the AI systems doing something wrong or harmful.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly relevant to investors and engineers — it's a new rule for how AI companies operate.

stories.title: State board approves artificial intelligence guidelines for K-12 schools, colleges
stories.simple_summary: A state board in Florida approved new rules for how schools and colleges should use and teach about artificial intelligence.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have grandchildren in Florida schools, they may learn about AI differently, but this is mainly for educators to follow.

stories.title: King Charles meets with artificial intelligence leaders over safety risks
stories.simple_summary: King Charles met with artificial intelligence leaders to discuss safety concerns about AI technology.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and politicians — it's the same message as other headlines: world leaders want AI to be safer.

stories.title: Microsoft AI CEO says AI threats are real, and Anthropic is making it worse
stories.simple_summary: The person in charge of AI at Microsoft says AI safety is a serious problem and criticized another major AI company.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly interesting to investors and tech industry people — different tech leaders disagree about how safe AI is right now.

stories.title: AI is feared globally as the destroyer of jobs
stories.simple_summary: A large survey asking over 42,000 people in 37 countries found that most people worry AI will take away their jobs.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own a small business or work, this shows many people are concerned about AI replacing workers — it's worth paying attention to how your industry changes.

stories.title: Chinese AI not powerful enough to see rogue-AI risks, says Huawei
stories.simple_summary: A Chinese company says that Chinese AI technology isn't advanced enough yet to understand some of the risks that very powerful AI could create.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and governments tracking AI progress — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Inside the suddenly explosive world of AI safety
stories.simple_summary: Top AI safety researchers met to investigate an incident where an unreleased AI system from a major company behaved in unexpected ways.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly for investors and engineers — it shows AI companies are discovering problems with how their AI systems work.

stories.title: How China is driving the emerging partisan divide on AI safety
stories.simple_summary: How different countries think about AI safety is becoming a topic that divides politicians along party lines.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly relevant to investors and politicians — it's a sign that AI regulation will become a political issue.

stories.title: OpenAI reveals 6 more incidents of "unexpected or concerning" AI behavior
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI reported six more times when their AI systems did something unexpected or concerning.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and engineers — it shows AI companies are finding problems with how their systems behave.

stories.title: Iceland-based Treble raises $18 million for its voice simulation platform
stories.simple_summary: A company called Treble that makes software to copy and create human voices raised $18 million from investors.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly relevant to investors — nothing you need to act on, though voice-copying technology exists and is getting better.
